base_member_text: [L9-L16] (MED/numeric-contract) The document asserts that XBeach uses double precision everywhere while describing the nonstandard `real*8` representation, but does not identify the compiler flags/kind policy that enforce this across the codebase.

[L18-L21,L34-L55] (MED/numeric-guidance) The guidance focuses on literal promotion but does not address modern kind-parameter practice or compiler-dependent literal evaluation, leaving the stated precision policy incomplete for portability.

[L89-L99] (LOW/performance-claim) The claim that an integer exponent is more efficient and that a real exponent may force `exp`/`log` is compiler/code-generation dependent and is presented without qualification or benchmark context.
[L126-L128] (LOW/documentation-quality) The explanatory parenthetical beginning at line 126 is not closed, making the final example structurally unclear.

audit_member_text: [L103-L107] (LOW/incorrect-numerical-example) The example identifies 1.2d0 as the intended nontruncated result of 5/4, but the correct value is 1.25d0.

[L72-L87] (LOW/unsupported-performance-distinction) The text attributes power-of-two multiplication and division optimizations to integer literal spelling even though the equivalent double-precision constants are exactly representable and can support the same optimizations.
